s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of respiratory and skin symptoms with a progressive rash
salient_findings: Pseudovesicular papules with superficial crusting on the trunk
key_facts: Age of the patient is in the 60s
Initial symptoms include asthenia, anorexia, and cough
Hospitalization occurred six days after symptom onset
Papules were asymptomatic and measured 3- to 6-mm
Papules evolved to a purpuric rash within 48 hours
Nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR tests for herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and SARS-CoV-2 were negative
Immunohistochemical testing for herpes simplex and varicella zoster viruses were negative
RT-PCR testing of fixed skin tissue for SARS-CoV-2 was negative
Histologic analysis showed extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis
Large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration were present
Dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis

shortlist.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis and large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive rash with purpuric evolution and mucocutaneous involvement

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic papules evolving to a purpuric rash and superficial crust

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Papulovesicular eruption with superficial crust and histologic findings of epidermal necrosis

shortlist.label: Henoch-Schönlein purpura
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric rash and dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including the rapid progression from papules to a purpuric rash and the histologic findings of extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis, are consistent with toxic epidermal necrolysis, a severe skin condition often associated with drug reactions or infections.

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
rejected.why: While similar to toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome typically involves less than 10% of the body surface area and often includes mucosal involvement, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is more common in children and is characterized by a staphylococcal toxin-mediated process, which is not indicated in the provided information.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: Erythema multiforme is characterized by target lesions and often involves mucosal surfaces, which does not align with the patient's presentation of papules evolving into a purpuric rash without mentioned mucosal involvement.

rejected.label: Henoch-Schönlein purpura
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by palpable purpura, abdominal pain, and arthritis, which are not mentioned in the vignette, and the histologic findings do not support vasculitis as seen in Henoch-Schönlein purpura.

gold: COVID-19-associated papulovesicular eruption with endotheliitis-like changes
